account: Sean Heelan is an independent vulnerability researcher who was auditing ksmbd, the Linux kernel's in-kernel server for the SMB3 file-sharing protocol. He used a known bug (CVE-2025-37778) to benchmark OpenAI's o3 through the plain application programming interface, with no scaffolding, agents or tools. Given about 12,000 lines covering all SMB command handlers, o3 reported a previously unknown use-after-free in the handler for the SMB “logoff” command. In that flaw, sess->user can be freed while another connection bound to the same session still uses it. Heelan wrote the fix on 21 April 2025. The SMB maintainer Steve French committed it to the kernel on 25 April 2025 with the acknowledgment of the ksmbd maintainer, Namjae Jeon. The fix reached the 6.12 and 6.14 branches in April and May 2025. The Linux kernel's CVE Numbering Authority published CVE-2025-37899 on 20 May 2025. Heelan's write-up followed on 22 May 2025. He calls it, to his knowledge, the first public case of a large language model finding a vulnerability of that nature. Linuxiac reported on 29 May 2025 that the upstream response was fast and that patches had been merged for every maintained branch. The fix reached the 6.1 and 6.6 longterm branches later, on 6 December 2025. The CVE record now describes the fix (“ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff”) with commits in five stable branches, and it lists fixed versions 6.1.159 and 6.6.119.

ai_role.statement: The model produced the finding unprompted during a benchmark. Heelan selected the code, validated the report and handled disclosure. He notes the model also produced false positives in other runs. The account is the independent deployer's own, corroborated by the CVE record and third-party coverage, not by OpenAI.

fields.account: Sean Heelan is an independent vulnerability researcher who was auditing ksmbd, the Linux kernel's in-kernel server for the SMB3 file-sharing protocol. He used a known bug (CVE-2025-37778) to benchmark OpenAI's o3 through the plain application programming interface, with no scaffolding, agents or tools. Given about 12,000 lines covering all SMB command handlers, o3 reported a previously unknown use-after-free in the handler for the SMB “logoff” command. In that flaw, sess->user can be freed while another connection bound to the same session still uses it. Heelan wrote the fix on 21 April 2025. The SMB maintainer Steve French committed it to the kernel on 25 April 2025 with the acknowledgment of the ksmbd maintainer, Namjae Jeon. The fix reached the 6.12 and 6.14 branches in April and May 2025. The Linux kernel's CVE Numbering Authority published CVE-2025-37899 on 20 May 2025. Heelan's write-up followed on 22 May 2025. He calls it, to his knowledge, the first public case of a large language model finding a vulnerability of that nature. Linuxiac reported on 29 May 2025 that the upstream response was fast and that patches had been merged for every maintained branch. The fix reached the 6.1 and 6.6 longterm branches later, on 6 December 2025. The CVE record now describes the fix (“ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff”) with commits in five stable branches, and it lists fixed versions 6.1.159 and 6.6.119.
